feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: clear positioning, solid career progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond web traffic, and slightly overpacked with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with logical progression at NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which strengthens credibility and leadership positioning.  
- Strong domain fit: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Writing is polished and concise overall, with no major misspellings or obvious typos; tone is professional and consistent.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact: include outcomes for email, social, video, campaigns, team leadership, budget scope, efficiency gains, or engagement improvements to strengthen impact.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (e.g., “content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs. lists without final commas); and keep punctuation/bullet formatting consistent, especially in long work-experience entries.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper specificity, a more concise opening, and less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner, more polished phrasing.
- Add one concrete scope marker from recent roles, e.g., enterprise web modernization, large-scale Drupal environments, or mission-driven membership organizations.
- Tighten broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” into a more senior framing focused on strategy, operations, and transformation.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social, and multimedia operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex communications programs. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout work experience; keep it, but avoid expanding it further here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It will be stronger if it emphasizes higher-value leadership and systems capabilities over broad communications phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic items with sharper, senior-level terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics and KPI reporting,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles, especially Drupal, platform migration, AI-enabled search, governance, and analytics infrastructure.
- Tighten style for consistency by using parallel noun phrases throughout.

Possible rewrite:
Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web governance • Editorial systems & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Data analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Stakeholder and cross-functional team leadership • Policy & advocacy messaging • Multimedia, livestream & event production • AI-enabled search & content discovery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” duplicates the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic advisory value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes/projects.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope and seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and cross-channel content operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on organization-wide communications effectiveness.
- Replace generic phrasing (“deliver CMS development,” “advise on best practices”) with outcome-oriented language: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular toolkit templates,” “Established governance and usability standards across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/templates launched, users supported, workflow time reduced, search/discovery improvements, or adoption by internal teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current bullets repeat website modernization, governance, analytics, and Drupal work already covered in the 2022–2024 NACo role.
- Specific project details on AI search and microsites also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for channels/studio/analytics: email engagement growth, production cost savings, faster reporting cycles, improved publishing compliance, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Tighten wording and use stronger verbs: “Established NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” and “Built analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either add distinct scale/results here or cut it.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as building enterprise capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and currently reads as a bridge role rather than a distinct step up. Emphasize what you owned at this level: operational leadership, newsletter scale, and launch/growth of recurring advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-led: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership where accurate: “Built/standardized editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/standards bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, executive-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise web and communications strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Editorial planning and content operations.”
- Reorder by strongest, most recent value: strategy, governance, cross-channel leadership, public-sector/advocacy communications.
- Use parallel phrasing and remove filler like “focused.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise web and communications strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and editorial planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple recent NACo bullets; keep this item concise rather than repeating channel details.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize platform leadership and execution strengths rather than repeat a full software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long tool inventory to a tighter capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older items here if they are not central to recent work, especially “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery,” since recent experience is clearly Drupal-led.
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “front-end implementation” or “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” for concision.
- If you want more impact, align to recent achievements: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “enterprise web modernization and AI-enabled search.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” from Core Competencies.
- Most platform/tool names are already covered in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the strategic value this topline area should signal. Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-focused, since the tools already appear elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a pure list.
- Emphasize higher-value skills first: KPI framework design, executive/leadership reporting, performance analysis, insight generation.
- Keep only 3–4 flagship platforms here; move the full stack to Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “- KPI and measurement framework design - Executive and leadership reporting - Web performance, SEO and user-behavior analysis - GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item substantially overlaps with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Listing both Microsoft Clarity and multiple BI tools here may be unnecessary unless they are central differentiators.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and make the phrasing more senior and outcomes-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ and multi-camera studio systems,” “Virtual event operations.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • In-house studio operations”
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools alone, e.g., “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, conferences, and recurring executive content.”
- Drop “editing” unless paired with strategy/ownership; otherwise it reads more tactical than the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine them into one stronger phrase.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or expanded with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, proven platforms: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If no qualifiers are added, keep only the most relevant 3–4 platforms to make the section sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and shorten/remove the other.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context or scale.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more current/senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward applied delivery: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Deployment.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript,” but consider dropping “jQuery” unless still actively relevant.
- Group by function for clarity: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “front-end troubleshooting,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless scripting” to better reflect current consulting/Drupal implementation work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider removing one version or making this section more tool-specific.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless implementation ownership is a key selling point.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal system-building rather than basic collaboration-tool familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to emphasize function: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Split by value/priority, leading with stronger technical tools: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration apps to a separate lower-priority line or drop weaker items: **Slack • Microsoft Teams**; consider removing **Basecamp** and **Trello** unless used recently or at depth
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a raw list, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing them may dilute stronger platform expertise.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/ownership implied elsewhere in the CV. It should better signal enterprise email platform leadership without repeating newsletter/channel claims already covered in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level of use: **Enterprise campaign setup, segmentation, journeys and newsletter operations in Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp**
- Keep platform names only if space is tight; otherwise use one concise descriptor that emphasizes systems capability over just software familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered well in the NACo experience entries.
- Be careful with “multi-channel communications” phrasing, which is already repeated in Core Competencies and Work Experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if known: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics such as “standardized publishing workflows” or “produced weekly advocacy videos and livestreamed major events.”
- Possible version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized multi-channel publishing workflows, produced weekly video updates and livestreamed key events, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Team leadership should stay light here since stronger management scope appears in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the distinctive innovation/research scope and tighten the media language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique contribution: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer outcome-oriented line, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia content to translate research and policy work into member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too close to later digital/media roles; keep this entry anchored in innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger leadership progression appears in later NACo roles.
